title: Event sequencing cards
subject: English
unit: Summer 1: Conflict poetry: power, memory and humanity
source: Seeded from english/y9 lesson 50 (Event sequencing cards (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 50: Non-fiction: the Battle of Balaklava. To understand how a historical article explains the causes and consequences of the charge, and how it complicates Tennyson's poem

cards:
consequence
the result of an action

ambiguous
having more than one possible
meaning

chain of command
the order of who gives orders
to whom
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Put the four cards in order
questions.a: Raglan writes the order; Nolan carries it; Lucan misreads it; Cardigan leads the charge.
questions.model: I do: I look for time words in the article (first, then, below) and place the order at the top.

questions.q: Why could Lord Lucan not understand the order?
questions.a: From the valley floor he could not see the guns Raglan meant, so 'the guns' was ambiguous.

questions.q: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'How do the article and the poem present responsibility for the charge?' Starter: 'The article names..., whereas Tennyson...'
questions.a: A PEEDL paragraph: the article names commanders and explains the error; Tennyson only says 'Someone had blunder'd' and focuses on honour.
questions.model: Point: The article and the poem treat responsibility very differently. | Evidence: the article traces the order from Raglan to Cardigan, while Tennyson writes only 'Someone had blunder'd'. | Explain: the historian wants accuracy; the poet wants commemoration. | Develop: by leaving 'Someone' unnamed, Tennyson keeps the focus on the men's courage. | Link: the poem is honest about the error but not about the blame.

questions.q: what does the poem leave out that the article includes?
questions.a: The names of commanders, the confusion of the order, the horses, the blame afterwards.

questions.q: is it fair for a poem to simplify history? Justify
questions.a: A balanced judgement on commemoration versus accuracy.

questions.q: Answer the ponder: who was responsible for the charge?
questions.a: For example: several commanders: the order was unclear and misread; the soldiers obeyed.
